title: Teacher English Placement Detailed CEFR Rubrics & Section Standards
notice: Objective sections (Listening, Grammar & Vocabulary, Reading) are scored automatically. Writing and Speaking are evaluated by an administrator using four 1–5 criteria (maximum 20 points).

bandScale.overall: Writing & Speaking: 4–6 = A1, 7–9 = A2, 10–13 = B1, 14–17 = B2, 18–20 = C1. Objective components are mapped to CEFR standard thresholds.

criteria.name: Main Idea & Gist Identification
criteria.description: Understanding core arguments, speaker stance, and primary purpose across academic conversations and announcements.

criteria.name: Specific Detail & Evidence Extraction
criteria.description: Capturing numerical data, exact dates, names, key conditions, and nuanced spoken facts without distraction.

criteria.name: Inference & Implicit Meaning
criteria.description: Deducing speaker tone, implied attitudes, indirect suggestions, and contextual nuance in spoken dialogue.

criteria.name: Syntactic Complexity & Sentence Structure
criteria.description: Accurate command of relative clauses, conditional sentences, passive structures, inversion, and subjunctive forms.

criteria.name: Collocation & Lexical Precision
criteria.description: Selection of natural academic vocabulary, phrasal combinations, appropriate registers, and nuanced word forms.

criteria.name: Tense & Aspect Consistency
criteria.description: Flawless application of perfect, continuous, and modal auxiliary systems in varied contextual scenarios.

criteria.name: Passage Synthesis & Global Comprehension
criteria.description: Interpreting complex expository and analytical prose, main themes, structural transitions, and thesis statements.

criteria.name: Evidence Scanning & Factual Verification
criteria.description: Locating specific evidence, corroborating claims, distinguishing facts from opinions, and analyzing data citations.

criteria.name: Lexical Inference & Contextual Meaning
criteria.description: Deciphering advanced academic vocabulary, figurative expressions, and references directly from context.

writing.title: Writing Evaluation Criteria
writing.weight: Administrator scores each criterion from 1 (A1) to 5 (C1) — Maximum 20 pts.
writing.reviewNote: Writing is evaluated via manual administrative rubric review across 4 core competencies.

criteria.name: Task Achievement
criteria.description: How fully the response addresses the prompt, presents a clear well-developed thesis, and substantiates arguments with relevant pedagogical and real-world evidence.

criteria.name: Coherence and Cohesion
criteria.description: How logically ideas are structured, utilizing effective paragraphing, precise referencing, smooth transitions, and diverse cohesive devices.

criteria.name: Lexical Resource
criteria.description: The range, sophistication, academic precision, flexibility of vocabulary, and idiomatic appropriacy with minimal lexical inaccuracies.

criteria.name: Grammatical Range and Accuracy
criteria.description: The variety of complex sentence structures, punctuation mastery, grammatical flexibility, and consistent error-free expression.

speaking.title: Speaking Evaluation Criteria
speaking.weight: Administrator scores each criterion from 1 (A1) to 5 (C1) — Maximum 20 pts.
speaking.reviewNote: Speaking is evaluated via candidate video/audio recordings across 4 core communicative parameters.

criteria.name: Fluency and Spontaneous Flow
criteria.description: Continuity of speech, natural pacing, effortless rhythm, logical continuity with minimal self-correction or unnatural hesitation.

criteria.name: Lexical Precision & Idiomatic Range
criteria.description: Range, precision, and sophistication of spoken vocabulary, using academic and conversational phrases naturally in context.

criteria.name: Grammatical Flexibility & Accuracy
criteria.description: Accuracy and versatility in deploying simple, compound, and complex sentence structures spontaneously.

criteria.name: Communication & Pronunciation Clarity
criteria.description: Pronunciation intelligibility, appropriate stress and intonation, clear articulation, and persuasive delivery of ideas.
